title: Frankie Newton, Bill Coleman, Bubber Miley, Howard Scott and Cootie
summary: He compares Newton and Coleman unfavorably to Stark's drive and praises Howard Scott's tone; the interview breaks off with Cootie Williams mentioned.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Now, how about somebody like Frankie Newton?
Well, I don't remember him in Chick's band.
No, no, I don't mean that. I just mean as a trumpeter.
Well, he was a good trumpet player. But there was something Frankie lacked in comparison with Bobby Stark. See, Bobby had that drive, which Frankie didn't have. Frankie was a good trumpet player.
He had interesting ideas, I thought.

Oh, he had wonderful ideas. But he didn't have that drive that Bobby had, you know. Yeah, Frankie played some beautiful things, wonderful. Just like Bill Coleman. I like Bill Coleman, too, as a trumpet player. But I mean, he was no comparison with Bobby Stark. And Bill could blow. Bill could blow.
Well, there was a lot of trumpet players. I can't even think of them now. New York was filled up with trumpet players, just like Metcalf and...
No, Red wasn't there then. Red, he didn't get here until '29. I'm talking about back around '27.
Oh, I see. All right, you had Bubber Miley.
Yeah, Bubber Miley. Yeah, there was quite a few trumpet players around. Scotty that was with Fletcher Henderson...

Howard Scott. He was never what you'd call a hot get-off man, but he was a beautiful-sounding trumpet player. He sounded like Joe Smith to me. Beautiful tone. Well, years go by and it's nice to think back to some of them fellows, you know. Have their names come back up in my mind -- with the help of you.
Cootie could really play, too, you said, when...
Cootie could play when he first come here with Alonzo Ross's band... Oh, I know I wanted to tell you something about...
